brief.title: The Last Audit
brief.premise: A junior scribe in the courts of the dead finds a mortal soul tallied to the wrong ledger column, and must carry the correction up through the counting-houses before the soul is weighed.
constraints: The dead cannot return to life; only their accounts move.

world.name: The Underworld Ledger
world.description: The dead are governed as an endless counting-house: every mortal life is tallied in ledgers, and each arriving soul is weighed against its account before it is allowed to rest.

locations.name: The Gate of Receipts
locations.description: The arrival gate where each soul surrenders its tally-slip and is queued for weighing.

locations.name: The Counting Halls
locations.description: Warrens of desks where scribes transcribe mortal lives into the ledgers.

locations.name: The Hall of Scales
locations.description: The weighing chamber where souls are measured against their ledger entries.

locations.name: The Erasure Wells
locations.description: Black shafts where accounts that cannot be balanced are dissolved.

locations.name: The Lamp Archive
locations.description: Sealed stacks holding the ledgers of the long dead, tended by lamplight.

factions.name: The Order of Scribes
factions.description: The clerks who transcribe mortal lives and vouch for every ledger entry.

factions.name: The Collegium of Weighers
factions.description: The officers who weigh souls and certify the balances.

factions.name: The Lamplighter Kin
factions.description: Keepers of the Lamp Archive and its sealed pages.

rules.statement: No soul returns to the living; the courts can only correct what is written.
A ledger correction stands only if sealed by three keys: a scribe, a weigher and a lamplighter.
A soul weighed against a miscast ledger is sent to the Erasure Wells.
A lamplighter who reads a sealed page aloud loses their lamp and their post.

history.name: The First Tally
history.description: The first ledger was opened so the dead could be judged by what was written, not by what was remembered.

history.name: The War of the Wrong Column
history.description: Rival weigher houses weighed the same souls twice over a column dispute, and the wells ran dark for a season.

history.name: The Lamp Seal
history.description: The three-key rule was instituted so no correction could be sealed by one office alone.

conflicts.name: The Miscast Harvest
conflicts.description: Miscast tallies are rising this count, and the scribes and weighers each blame the other's desk.

conflicts.name: The Sealed Ledgers
conflicts.description: The lamplighters refuse to open sealed ledgers for the audit without a weigher's warrant.

characters.name: Itho Pel
characters.description: A junior scribe of the Counting Halls who copies mortal accounts and notices errors his seniors prefer to overlook.
characters.motivation: To see the soul weighed against what it actually did.
characters.goal: Get the miscast entry corrected and triple-sealed before the weighing.
characters.flaw: He trusts ink more than people, and says so.
characters.internal_conflict: Correcting the ledger means accusing the offices that feed him.
characters.external_conflict: The weighers' collegium bars a junior scribe from the scales.

abilities.name: Fault-sight
abilities.description: Spots a mis-tallied column at a glance, the way a proof-reader spots a dropped letter.

characters.arc: Itho learns that a correction is only ink until three unwilling hands agree to seal it.

characters.name: Dame Ors
characters.description: A senior weigher of the collegium who certified the miscast harvest of tallies and guards the scales' reputation as her own.
characters.motivation: To protect the weighers' infallibility, on which the whole court rests.
characters.goal: Quash the audit and weigh the soul as written.
characters.internal_conflict: She knows the column is wrong and has convinced herself the error is small.
characters.external_conflict: Itho's correction would put her seal beside the error.

abilities.name: Scale-craft
abilities.description: Reads a soul's weight to the last dram and detects a doctored balance.

characters.arc: Dame Ors must choose between the scales' honesty and her own.

characters.name: Hemo Lux
characters.description: A lamplighter archivist who tends the sealed stacks and remembers the index of every ledger he is forbidden to read.
characters.motivation: To keep the archive honest without breaking his lamp oath.
characters.goal: Produce the matching archive entry without reading a sealed page.
characters.flaw: He hides behind procedure when courage would serve better.
characters.internal_conflict: His oath protects the dead but shelters the fraud.
characters.external_conflict: Dame Ors threatens his lamp if he assists the audit.

abilities.name: Index memory
abilities.description: Recalls the position and cross-references of any sealed ledger without opening it.

characters.arc: Hemo risks his lamp to give the correction its third key.

relationships.description: Hemo's index can find the matching entry that proves the miscast.
relationships.conflict: Helping Itho puts Hemo's lamp in jeopardy.

relationships.description: Dame Ors certified the harvest of tallies Itho is auditing.
relationships.conflict: Her seal is required for the correction she wants buried.

evidence_summary: The world, cast and storyboard satisfy the brief's bureaucratic afterlife setting; deterministic validators are clean and there are no blocking defects.
